items.title: Getting started
items.description: What happens the first time you run DeskDrawer, and the four things worth doing in your first five minutes.

items.title: Installing DeskDrawer
items.description: System requirements, what installing actually puts on your machine, and how updates and autostart work.

items.title: Boards
items.description: Creating, naming, moving, resizing, folding and deleting boards — and what a board stores.

items.title: Menus
items.description: DeskDrawer has three menus: its own board menu, its tray menu, and the real Windows context menu. Knowing which is which explains most of the interface.

items.title: Sorting a board
items.description: Five sort modes, each ascending or descending, set independently per board.

items.title: Icon sizes
items.description: DeskDrawer offers four icon sizes, set independently for each board, and re-tiles the layout automatically when you change one.

items.title: Keyboard and mouse reference
items.description: Every gesture and shortcut on a board. Most of them are the ones you already use on the Windows desktop.

items.title: Drag and drop
items.description: What each kind of drag does, when a file actually moves on disk, and the safeguards around that.

items.title: Layout and multiple monitors
items.description: How boards behave across several displays, mixed DPI scaling, resolution changes and taskbar moves.

items.title: Languages and language independence
items.description: DeskDrawer's Store listing is available in 16 languages, and the application itself is designed so that using it depends very little on reading text at all.

items.title: The configuration file
items.description: Where DeskDrawer keeps your layout, what is in it, how it is written safely, and whether you should edit it.

items.title: Backup, restore and moving to a new PC
items.description: Copying one file backs up your entire layout. What transfers cleanly to another machine and what does not.

items.title: Privacy and local data
items.description: What DeskDrawer stores, what it transmits, and the specific list of things it does not contain.

items.title: Uninstalling
items.description: How to remove DeskDrawer cleanly, what is left behind (nothing), and how to get your desktop icons back.

items.title: Architecture
items.description: How DeskDrawer is put together: one process, no services, WinForms over the Windows shell, and the reasoning behind each of those choices.

items.title: Windows integration
items.description: The specific Windows behaviours DeskDrawer hooks into — the desktop icon layer, Show desktop, Alt+F4, the Share pane, the Recycle Bin — and how each is made to behave correctly.

items.title: Performance
items.description: What DeskDrawer does to stay responsive on large, cloud-backed and network-connected desktops — and what can still make it slow.

items.title: Memory usage
items.description: What DeskDrawer holds in memory, the choices that keep that small, and how to measure it on your own machine.

items.title: Limitations
items.description: What DeskDrawer does not do, what it will not do, and the rough edges that are known and unfixed.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.description: Fixes for the problems that actually come up: missing icons, misplaced boards, freezes, an empty desktop, and startup not sticking.

items.title: Licensing and purchase
items.description: How the one-time purchase works, what it covers, how many machines it installs on, and why no price appears on this site.
